value: Acceleration stays constant (g) throughout free fall
reasoning: An object falling freely moves only under gravity, so its acceleration is g at every instant, even at the top of its path where the velocity is momentarily zero. That rules out C, and A is false because a body can move at constant velocity with zero acceleration.

If two field lines crossed, the field at the crossing point would have two directions at once, which is impossible. Magnetic field lines are also closed loops, so they do not originate or terminate at a point.

value: Left-hand rule gives the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
reasoning: Fleming's left-hand rule (motor rule) gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. The right-hand rule (dynamo rule) gives the direction of induced current, not the force.

value: Every simple harmonic motion is periodic
reasoning: Simple harmonic motion repeats itself after a fixed time period, so it is always periodic. The converse fails: many periodic motions, such as the Earth's orbit or a bouncing ball, are not simple harmonic.
A speed radar gun measures the change in frequency of waves reflected from a moving vehicle; the frequency shift is proportional to the vehicle's speed. This is the Doppler effect.

value: The claim that the third law implies a cause-effect relation is the incorrect statement
reasoning: Action and reaction act simultaneously, so neither is the cause of the other; the third law implies no cause-effect relation. Forces always occur in pairs (A), and the stone does pull the Earth (B), so C is the false statement.

value: Fireworks, to give a bright white light
reasoning: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white light, which is why it is used in fireworks, flares and flash powder. Examining the alimentary canal uses barium sulphate, and gemstones are not magnesium products.

value: Thiourea as an accelerator is not a paint ingredient
reasoning: Paint consists of a pigment (such as titanium dioxide), a vehicle or drying oil, a thinner (such as turpentine), driers, anti-skinning agents (such as polyhydroxy phenols) and extenders. Accelerators like thiourea belong to rubber vulcanisation, not paint.

value: Ruby's red colour is not due to beryllium (it is due to chromium)
reasoning: Ruby is aluminium oxide coloured red by traces of chromium; beryllium is found in emerald and beryl, so D is false. Runner-up B: strictly it is barium sulphate, not barium metal, that is used as the X-ray contrast meal, so B is also loosely worded, but D is the clear intended false statement.

Neon glows a characteristic orange-red when an electric discharge passes through it, which is why it is used in red advertising signs. Helium gives a pinkish-yellow glow and argon a lavender-blue one.

Permanent hardness comes from chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, which boiling cannot remove. An ion-exchange resin (or zeolite) swaps these Ca and Mg ions for sodium or hydrogen ions. Boiling and lime treatment (Clark's method) remove only temporary hardness.

value: Polyaromatic hydrocarbons are not a photochemical smog component
reasoning: Photochemical smog contains ozone, nitric oxide, PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate), acrolein and formaldehyde, formed when sunlight acts on nitrogen oxides and hydrocarbons. Polyaromatic hydrocarbons are soot and combustion particulates, not standard smog constituents. Runner-up D would win only if nitric oxide were treated as a precursor rather than a component, but it is listed as a component.
Eukaryotic chromatin is DNA wrapped around basic histone proteins to form nucleosomes, along with non-histone proteins. DNA and protein are its essential components.

Flatworms (Platyhelminthes) are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and acoelomate. Porifera have cellular organisation and Cnidaria are radially symmetrical and diploblastic, while Annelida have a true coelom.
Gaseous exchange takes place across the thin walls of the alveoli, the air sacs richly supplied with capillaries. The nasal passage, trachea and bronchi only conduct air.

Adrenaline, secreted directly into the blood by the adrenal glands, speeds up the heartbeat to prepare the body for emergencies. Insulin regulates blood sugar and testosterone governs male characteristics.

value: Nerve endings of the nerve cell
reasoning: Neurotransmitters are stored in vesicles at the nerve endings (axon terminals) and released into the synaptic cleft when an impulse arrives. Runner-up D: textbooks describe the release at the end of the axon, which is the same place; C is the more exact choice.
Platelets (thrombocytes) release factors that start the clotting of blood at a wound. Oxygen transport is the role of red blood cells, while immunity and phagocytosis belong to white blood cells.

The de Broglie wavelength is \(\lambda = h/p\), so equal wavelengths mean equal momentum. Their energies and speeds still differ, since a photon travels at c and its energy is pc, while the electron's energy is p squared over 2m.

Among the options, oil and water stay separate because of surface (interfacial) tension: the cohesive forces within each liquid are stronger than the attraction between them, so a boundary forms. The deeper reason is that water is polar and oil non-polar, but no option names this, and the others are plainly unrelated.

value: Solid, liquid and vapour phases all co-exist
reasoning: The triple point is the unique temperature and pressure at which the solid, liquid and vapour phases of a substance co-exist in equilibrium (for water, 273.16 K and about 611 Pa).

Latent heat is the heat absorbed or released during a change of state without any change in temperature. Volume changes during a phase change, so D is wrong. Runner-up C: a phase change also normally happens at constant pressure, but the defining property taught is constant temperature.

value: The claim that kinetic energy does not change with frequency is incorrect
reasoning: By Einstein's equation, the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons equals \(h\nu - h\nu_0\), so it increases with the frequency of the incident light. The other statements are true: Einstein's 1921 Nobel was for this work, a threshold frequency exists, and the number of electrons is proportional to intensity.
Chlorine occurs as Cl-35 (about 75%) and Cl-37 (about 25%). The weighted average is 35 x 0.75 + 37 x 0.25 = 35.5 u.

Tropolone is a seven-membered carbocyclic, non-benzenoid aromatic compound with no heteroatom in its ring. Furan (oxygen), thiophene (sulphur) and pyridine (nitrogen) all carry a heteroatom in an aromatic ring.
Bauxite is hydrated aluminium oxide, the ore of aluminium, and contains no silicate framework. Feldspar, zeolite and mica are all naturally occurring aluminosilicates.
Glycolysis, the breakdown of glucose into two molecules of pyruvate, takes place in the cytoplasm. Pyruvate then enters the mitochondria for aerobic respiration.

value: Ovule becomes the seed and ovary becomes the fruit
reasoning: After fertilisation the ovule develops into the seed, and the ovary enlarges and ripens into the fruit enclosing it.

value: Glucose breaks down to CO2, water and energy in aerobic tissues
reasoning: Aerobic respiration completely oxidises glucose to carbon dioxide, water and energy. A fails because anaerobic organisms do not do this, B fails because muscles produce lactic acid, not ethanol, and D fails because yeast produces ethanol and CO2, not lactate.

Intercropping is growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in a definite row pattern. Crop rotation is growing different crops one after another in successive seasons on the same field.

In May 2020 Sania Mirza won the Fed Cup Heart Award for the Asia/Oceania zone, becoming the first Indian to receive it. The other three are a badminton player, another badminton player and a sprinter, not tennis players.
National Technology Day is observed on 11 May, marking the Pokhran-II nuclear tests of 11 May 1998 and the first flight of the Hansa-3 aircraft on the same day.
Under Mission Sagar, INS Kesari sailed on 10 May 2020 carrying food items, COVID-related medicines and medical teams to the Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles, Madagascar and Comoros.

In the 2019-20 Budget Estimates, corporation tax was the largest single item of the Centre's gross tax revenue at about 7.66 lakh crore rupees, ahead of the Centre's GST collections (about 6.6 lakh crore including compensation cess) and income tax. Runner-up A: GST would win if the State share or a different estimate were counted.
MSME stands for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, the sector governed by the MSMED Act, 2006.

Sweden topped the World Economic Forum's Energy Transition Index in 2020 for the third year running, followed by Switzerland. The '74th' in the stem appears to be India's rank in that index, so the wording is odd, but the top-ranked country is Sweden.
Operation Sadbhavana is the Indian Army's civic action programme in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, running schools, health care and infrastructure projects to win the goodwill of local people.
A Wing Commander in the Indian Air Force is equivalent to a Lieutenant Colonel in the Army and a Commander in the Navy. Captain matches Flight Lieutenant, and Colonel matches Group Captain.

The MNRE 'Development of Solar Cities' programme aimed at a minimum 10 per cent reduction in the projected demand of conventional energy at the end of five years, through energy efficiency and renewable energy. Runner-up B (5 per cent) would be right only if the scheme set a lower target than I recall.
The name Amphan (meaning sky) was contributed by Thailand to the North Indian Ocean cyclone naming list prepared in 2004; it was the last name on that list.
Natural population change (natural increase) is the difference between births and deaths, calculated as crude birth rate minus crude death rate, ignoring migration.

A spit is a ridge of sand or shingle attached to the mainland at one end and projecting into the sea. A bar is not attached at either end (or closes a bay), and a tombolo links an island to the mainland.

Coral reefs support fishing and tourism jobs, supply coral limestone used as building material, and act as natural breakwaters against storm waves. They offer no protection from earthquakes, which originate within the crust.

Dardic languages such as Kashmiri and Shina belong to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European family.
Census 2011 divides workers into four categories: cultivators, agricultural labourers, household industry workers and other workers. 'Domestic workers' is not one of them.

Percentage change in quantity = (20 - 30)/30 = -33.3 per cent; percentage change in price = (15 - 12)/12 = 25 per cent. Elasticity = 33.3/25 = 1.33 in absolute value, so demand is elastic.

Food inflation is measured over food items such as cereals (wheat, paddy and rice) and sugar. Tobacco is not a food item: it is classed with pan and intoxicants or non-food articles, so it is excluded. Only option D leaves out tobacco.

The steatite seal is described as the most distinctive artefact of the Harappan civilisation, and bricks of a standard 1:2:4 ratio are another hallmark found across all its sites. Gold bangles and silver spittoons are not distinctive Harappan items. Runner-up A (1 only) wins if only the seal, as the single 'most distinctive' artefact, is counted.
The sixteen mahajanapadas of the Buddhist and Jaina lists include Kuru, Vatsa and Gandhara, but not Kalinga. Kalinga became prominent later, notably in the Mauryan period.

reasoning: The Dharmashastras assign Vaishyas the duties of studying the Vedas, performing sacrifices and giving gifts, along with agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade. Both statements are therefore prescribed duties.

value: The claim that fundamental duties cannot be used to judge constitutionality is incorrect
reasoning: Courts may refer to the fundamental duties when deciding whether a law is reasonable and constitutional, so D is false. A is true (they were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976), B is true (Article 51A), and C is true because they are non-justiciable.

value: Class divisions being irremediable is not a socialist belief
reasoning: Socialists see class divisions as a product of private ownership that can and should be overcome, so calling them irremediable contradicts socialism. Emphasis on community, distribution by need and concern with inequality of income are socialist ideas.

Airports Authority of India is a Miniratna (Category I) CPSU. Indian Oil Corporation and SAIL are Maharatnas, and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited is a Navratna.
Since 2010 the HDI's education dimension uses mean years of schooling (adults 25 and above) and expected years of schooling, replacing the earlier adult literacy and gross enrolment measures.
Adam Smith's 'invisible hand' is the market or price mechanism, through which self-interested buyers and sellers are guided to allocate resources efficiently without central direction.

The CACP recommends the Minimum Support Price for wheat and rice, a floor price at which the government stands ready to buy, so it is a support price. India's mobile telecom market is dominated by a few large operators (Jio, Airtel and Vodafone Idea, with BSNL), whose pricing decisions are interdependent. That is an oligopoly.
